steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-28, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 853.6 | 0.80 | 0.80
2 | 1156.2 | 1.92 | 2.72
3 | 234.7 | 7.57 | 10.29
4 | 2817.0 | 39.25 | 49.54
5 | 234.7 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-28, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station T-28 (Area T)**

A 5-layer geoelectric model was delineated from the VES data:
- **Layer 1:** 853.6 Ω·m, thickness 0.80 m (base at 0.80 m)
- **Layer 2:** 1156.2 Ω·m, thickness 1.92 m (base at 2.72 m)
- **Layer 3:** 234.7 Ω·m, thickness 7.57 m (base at 10.29 m)
- **Layer 4:** 2817.0 Ω·m, thickness 39.25 m (base at 49.54 m)
- **Layer 5:** 234.7 Ω·m, semi-infinite basement conductor

Evaluating the consecutive layer triplets:
1. Layers 1–2–3: $\rho_1 < \rho_2 > \rho_3 \rightarrow \text{K}$
2. Layers 2–3–4: $\rho_2 > \rho_3 < \rho_4 \rightarrow \text{H}$
3. Layers 3–4–5: $\rho_3 < \rho_4 > \rho_5 \rightarrow \text{K}$

The sequence yields a **KHK** curve type, confirming that the recorded classification on file is correct.
